Jules picked up an old elementary school project where he'd constructed a cardboard castle using scraps from craft week. He recalled how happy it was supposed to make him. Next to the castle's remains lay an exercise of handwriting – childishly sloppy letters spelling out rhyming poems. Every piece spoke volumes about his... past.

As Jules turned over her childhood works – or rather, hers and his mother's joint ones – he heard something strange: a voice from inside him was speaking out against this whole experience without saying anything at all. Silence was its argument – an unsettling silence that seethed within him like static electricity building towards some massive release.

Forcing a breath into lungs gone too still, Jules forced down the urge to flee, instead pushing a heavy box off its shelf with enough force to rumble the whole wooden framework of memories built around them all. But even as the boxes tumbled from their shelf – releasing their dusty burden into chaos – the disquiet in his soul refused release.
